speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any fever, joint pain, or recent illness before the blisters appeared? Also, have you started any new medications or supplements recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the oral and genital ulcers, I need to rule out autoimmune blistering diseases. Have you noticed any skin lesions that are painful rather than itchy, and do you have a history of easy bruising or bleeding gums? REQUEST TEST: Skin Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Histopathology: Acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy showing acantholysis is highly suggestive of Pemphigus Vulgaris. Do you have any history of smoking, and have you noticed any loose teeth or gum bleeding? REQUEST TEST: Direct Immunofluorescence

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of mucosal ulcers and blisters, combined with biopsy findings of acantholysis and direct immunofluorescence showing intercellular IgG and C3 deposition, is diagnostic for Pemphigus Vulgaris. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris
